topic: software supply chain; cybersecurity; access control; dependency ecosystems
status: bounded synthesis of four fixed-frame random full-text audits; taxonomy/evaluation-design hypothesis, not field prevalence
claim: The sampled `software_supply_chain` label currently combines distinct threat surfaces and evidence types: smartcard command interleaving, OS sandboxing of R, database inference control, and observational dependency-network evolution. Their outcomes—silent command anomalies, selected sandbox tests, a theorem conditional on policy inputs, and historical graph statistics—cannot be pooled as one security-effectiveness trend. The broad label remains useful for discovery, but should be decomposed before candidate scoring or evidence synthesis.
positive_evidence: The smartcard study tests two physical devices and demonstrates command interleaving that can complete without warning; it does not estimate attack prevalence.
RAppArmor demonstrates selected Linux/AppArmor restrictions in unit tests and explicitly presents itself as a proof of concept.
The access-control paper proves a conditional non-inference result given a specified schema and sensitive-attribute policy, and proposes DBMS integration as future work.
The seven-ecosystem study analyzes package dependency graph structure and fragility, not attacks, vulnerabilities, or compromise outcomes.
counterevidence: These domains all concern security risks in software systems and a broad recall-oriented discovery tag can legitimately include them.
The sample is small and only four of twelve random keys in this topic have been audited; it cannot estimate bucket-wide contamination or field prevalence.
The historical dependency study covers seven ecosystems and millions of package records, offering broad observational evidence within its own graph-structure question.
falsifiable_test: Blindly double-annotate a probability sample of at least 100 records from the retrieval bucket by asset/threat surface (dependency/provenance, runtime isolation, hardware/firmware, privacy/inference, incident/attack, other) and evidence design (theorem, lab demonstration, test suite, observational ecosystem data, deployment study). Report agreement and bucket precision for each class; then compare candidate rankings before and after stratification. The concern weakens if independent annotations converge on one outcome family and within-family measures support stable pooled claims.
limitations: Only four records from two early time strata are audited here; eight unread records and most recent-period cases may materially alter the taxonomy. No meta-analysis or causal estimate is appropriate.
